title: What defiles (Matthew 15:1–20)
hookLine: clean hands in seconds; what about what comes out of the mouth?
tomorrow: what if you keep asking, and the answer is silence?

cards: The pump by the door, the sharp smell of alcohol, the cold on your palms, then gone. Clean hands in a few seconds. Matthew has a scene that begins with hands at a table.

Visitors come from Jerusalem, Pharisees and scribes, with a serious question about a practice handed down: "Why do thy disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? for they wash not their hands when they eat bread."
It's an argument among Jews about how to keep God's ways, and Jesus answers by pointing further in.

teach.b: First he quotes the prophet Isaiah: "This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me." Lips close, heart far.

Then he turns to the crowd: "Hear, and understand: Not that which goeth into the mouth defileth a man; but that which cometh out of the mouth, this defileth a man." Peter, being Peter, asks what that means.
What goes in passes through the body.

teach.h: WHAT COMES OUT, FROM THE HEART.
teach.b: But "those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart; and they defile the man. For out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, blasphemies."
Here's the detail worth telling a friend: the first thing on that list isn't a deed at all. It's thoughts. Before anything reaches the hands or the mouth, it starts further in.

And Matthew ends right back at the table: "These are the things which defile a man: but to eat with unwashen hands defileth not a man." The question in this chapter isn't whether your hands are clean.
It's what's coming up from the heart.

how: Some Christians pray Psalm 51's line, create in me a clean heart, O God, and in some churches it is sung during worship.

o: touching something unclean at the temple
breaking a rule of the Roman authorities
what comes out of the heart, not what goes in

s: the visitors' question was about germs and hygiene
they asked about the tradition of the elders: why the disciples ate without washing.
the first thing on Jesus' list is a deed, like theft
out of the heart proceed evil thoughts first; deeds come after.
Jesus answers with words from the prophet Isaiah
"This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth... but their heart is far from me."

games.q: you scrub the kitchen spotless before guests arrive, snapping at your family the whole time. what would Matthew 15 point to?
o: the clean kitchen: welcoming guests well comes first.
the snapping: what comes out starts in the heart.
nothing: stress makes everyone snap a little.
games.why: Jesus says what comes out of the mouth comes forth from the heart, and that's what defiles. a clean surface can sit right beside a sharp tongue.

practice: Rub your palms together slowly, as if you were washing them, and feel the warmth come. Then lay one hand flat on your chest and feel it rise and fall with your breath.
Leave it there, and notice what's been coming up from in there today: a sharp word, a kind one, a worry.

wordCard.voice: What defiles. In Matthew 15, not what goes into the mouth, but what comes out of it, from the heart.

orig.note: Greek for heart, in Matthew 15:8 and 15:18–19: out of the heart proceed evil thoughts.

carryVoice: Your line: from the heart. Words travel out, but they start further in. Until tomorrow.
